finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id calls authorized() and discards its boolean return value, so any authenticated user can delete any project they do not own.
finding.source: req.params.id (api.js:17) and req.user; any authenticated non-owner, non-admin user reaching the route.

trace.note: project loaded by attacker-supplied ID with no ownership filter
authorized(req.user, project) called; return value ignored; predicate never throws
authorized() only returns a boolean (resource.ownerId === user.id || user.isAdmin === true)

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 is a non-throwing predicate whose result is discarded. authorize() at api.js:4-10 would throw 403 but is not called on this route. The PUT /projects/:id/name route at api.js:25 correctly uses authorize(). Route-level authentication middleware is not in this directory, so whether req.user is always populated could not be confirmed; this affects reachability, not the missing ownership check.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean, and its result is discarded by the bare call at api.js:18. authorize() at api.js:4-10 would throw 403, but the DELETE route never calls it. No ownership filter at api.js:17 and no route-level check in this directory.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls authorized(req.user, project) as a bare statement, so its false return at api.js:13 never stops the unconditional delete at api.js:19, and the attacker is any authenticated low-privilege user who can reach the route, since api.js:12-13 and the route at api.js:16 show no role gate. The only unverified part is whether req.user is always populated, which is outside this directory and affects reachability only.
